request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Mithril Protocol continuous development and Intersect budget administration.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 3,810,423 ada, consisting of 3,699,440 ada for Mithril Protocol Continuous Development and 110,983 ada for the Intersect Budget Administration fee.
Mithril uses stake-based threshold multi-signatures to certify Cardano state in a trustless way so nodes and applications can verify state rapidly without relying on the entire chain.
Mithril is presented as fully aligned with Infrastructure & Research Excellence and Adoption & Utility, and partially aligned with Community & Ecosystem Growth.
The proposer states that Mithril can reduce dependency on centralized indexers and hosted APIs as Cardano faces governance activity, ecosystem expansion, and scaling pressure.

The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain Treasury Withdrawal submission under the approved Budget Process Framework.
The proposer states that the requested amount does not, at submission time alone or in aggregate, breach the 350M ada Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.

Audit and oversight costs are included in the proposal overhead, with independent oversight planned through Intersect and technically capable third parties, reporting obligations, and milestone-based disbursement controls.
Teragone has not previously received direct funding from Cardano treasury or community governance programs, while its Mithril work to date has been funded by IOG through close collaboration.

Intersect will manage withdrawn funds through a 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract and one Project-Specific Smart Contract using stated addresses, multisignature role thresholds, external oversight entities, and a public dashboard.

The proposal provides references to the Intersect budget vote, voting documentation, audited results, smart contract guide, smart contract repository, and audit reports for the budget management contracts.

summary: The document requests 3,810,423 ada for Mithril Protocol continuous development via Intersect-administered treasury smart contracts, with budget-process references, NCL compliance assertions, oversight arrangements, and a high-level budget split, but it provides limited detail on concrete Mithril milestones, delivery schedule, or cost basis.
